items.real_world_notes: New for the general store (GAME_DESIGN 5.7, added 2026-10-09): warmth at camp, heavy, and a flat-lay backdrop once owned (6.1). Off the shelf until the wool_blanket switch turns on (BUILD_PLAN 3.6, M1b). Every number is an estimate: weight and price from 5.7's table (the plain version), the rest from sweater_wool_vintage and liner_fleece.

items.name: Unscented Wet Wipes (pack out)
items.real_world_notes: A camp 'shower'. They never decompose: every used wipe gets packed out.
items.flavor: Damp little cloths that make a dusty face feel almost clean again.

items.name: Deodorant Stick
items.real_world_notes: A smellable that takes canister space and attracts curious animals. The forest does not mind how you smell.
items.flavor: A sweet-smelling stick that the squirrels find more interesting than you do.

items.name: Paperback Book
items.real_world_notes: The tent-bound rainy afternoon's best friend.
items.flavor: A paperback with soft corners, for reading in the tent while the rain drums its fingers on the roof.

items.name: Harmonica
items.real_world_notes: Light music at camp; keep it soft and short where other campers are close.
items.flavor: A little silver harmonica, for playing a slow tune while the sun goes down.

items.name: Travel Ukulele
items.real_world_notes: Camp songs at the lake. Rides outside the pack and snags on everything.
items.flavor: A small four-stringed guitar that turns any campsite into a concert hall.

items.name: Melodica
items.real_world_notes: A small keyboard you play by blowing through a mouthpiece or a short tube. A 32-key one weighs about 20 oz alone and about 2 lb in its soft case, which is about 20 in long; 37-key ones run 19 to 25 oz. Reedy and loud enough to carry across a still lake, so keep it soft and short where other campers are close.
items.flavor: A little keyboard you play by blowing into it, which sounds like an accordion that went to summer camp.

items.name: Bigleaf Dreadnought Guitar
items.real_world_notes: A full-size dreadnought, the big steel-string acoustic: about 4.5 lb alone, about 41 in long, nearly 16 in across the lower bout and 5 in deep. In a padded gig bag it is about 7.5 lb and about 70 L, bigger than most whole backpacks, so it rides strapped to the outside and catches every branch and gust; a hard case would add 8 to 14 lb. A solid-wood one costs about $1,000 to $2,000 new. Backpackers who want music usually carry a travel guitar or a ukulele; this is the loud, rich-sounding choice, and the heavy, awkward one. The maker is fictional.
items.flavor: A big full-size guitar that bumps every tree on the way in, then makes the whole camp go quiet to listen.

items.name: Deck of Playing Cards
items.real_world_notes: Rainy-day entertainment for two or more.
items.flavor: A deck of cards for long, rainy afternoons and friendly arguments.

items.name: Flying Disc
items.real_world_notes: Wonderful on a wide coastal beach at low tide; pointless in a dense forest camp.
items.flavor: A plastic disc that sails across the beach like a gull.

items.name: Fixed-Line Fly Fishing Kit
items.real_world_notes: No Washington fishing license is needed inside the park, but park rules apply: artificial lures and flies only, single barbless hooks, and catch-and-release for native species in many waters. Check the current park fishing regulations.
items.flavor: A long, thin rod that folds into a tube, for casting a tiny fly onto a quiet lake.

items.name: Telescoping Spinning Rod and Lures
items.real_world_notes: Bulkier than a fly kit; lures must be single barbless hooks under park rules. Bait is generally not allowed.
items.flavor: A rod that slides out long and shiny, for trying your luck where the trout rise.

items.name: Compact Binoculars
items.real_world_notes: More marmots, elk, mountain goats, eagles and whales (from the coast in spring). Spot the route across a far snowfield.
items.flavor: Two little telescopes that bring the marmots and eagles close enough to say hello.

items.name: Compact Camera
items.real_world_notes: Better photos than a phone, with zoom for wildlife. Batteries drain fast in the cold. A compact's battery is rated for roughly 300-400 shots (CIPA); about two days of trail photos, less in the cold.
items.flavor: A small camera for catching rainbows and elk and the light on the mountains.

items.name: Big Camera with Zoom Lens
items.real_world_notes: Glorious photos and two and a half pounds of fragile glass. Rain and fords are its enemies. A DSLR battery is rated for roughly 800-1,000 shots (CIPA): about four days of photos.
items.flavor: A heavy camera with a long lens, for photographers who don't mind a heavy pack.

items.name: Disposable Film Camera
items.real_world_notes: Twenty-seven shots, no screen, and a surprise when the prints come back after the trip.
items.flavor: A paper-and-plastic camera that keeps its pictures secret until you get home.

items.name: Star Chart Wheel
items.real_world_notes: Away from city lights, the High Divide and the coast show the Milky Way in late summer.
items.flavor: A turning wheel of stars that shows which ones are shining over your tent tonight.

items.name: Portable Wireless Speaker
items.real_world_notes: Music played aloud ruins the quiet for everyone and scares wildlife away. Leave No Trace includes sound; use earbuds or listen to the river instead. Small speakers run about 10-15 hours on a charge.
items.flavor: A little speaker that is loud enough to make the marmots and the neighbors leave.

items.name: Mini Camera Drone
items.real_world_notes: Launching, landing or operating drones anywhere on Olympic's lands or waters is prohibited (as in national parks generally). Expect a ranger conversation, a citation and grounded footage. A mini drone flies about 30 minutes per battery.
items.flavor: A buzzing little flying camera that is not allowed to fly anywhere in this park.

items.name: Wooden Flower Press
items.real_world_notes: Picking plants and flowers in a national park is prohibited. Leave the flower where it grows.
items.flavor: Two little wooden boards for pressing flowers, which the mountain would rather keep.

items.name: Pocket Sketchbook
items.real_world_notes: A small, sturdy sketchbook. Drawing what you find, rather than collecting it, is the oldest Leave No Trace keepsake.
items.flavor: A little book of empty pages, waiting for a flower that no one has ever drawn.

items.name: Drawing Pencils, Eraser and Sharpener
items.real_world_notes: Pencils work in the rain when pens won't.
items.flavor: Three pencils, soft and hard, and a small eraser for second thoughts.

items.name: Watercolor Pencils (12 colors)
items.real_world_notes: Draw dry, then touch with a wet brush, or simply with a drop of rain.
items.flavor: Twelve colors, from moss green to sunset gold.

items.name: Travel Watercolor Kit with Water Brush
items.real_world_notes: A palm-sized pan set; the water brush holds its own water. Rinse water goes 200 ft from lakes.
items.flavor: A tiny box of paints and a brush that carries its own water, for painting the sky.

items.name: Waterproof Field Notebook and Pen
items.real_world_notes: Writes in the rain. For trip notes, plant lists and the names of new friends.
items.flavor: A notebook that doesn't mind the rain, for writing down everything you see.

items.name: Field Guide to Northwest Wildflowers
items.real_world_notes: Names the avalanche lilies, lupines, paintbrush, and Olympic endemics such as Piper's bellflower and Flett's violet.
items.flavor: A book full of flowers, with one page still waiting for a picture.

items.name: Field Guide to Trees, Ferns and Mosses
items.real_world_notes: Sitka spruce or western hemlock? Licorice fern or sword fern? Turns the rain forest into a library.
items.flavor: A guide to the tall trees and the soft green things that grow all over them.

items.name: Field Guide to Birds and Mammals
items.real_world_notes: Gray jays, ravens, sooty grouse, Olympic marmots (found nowhere else on Earth), elk and black bears.
items.flavor: A book of feathers, fur, and footprints.

items.name: Field Guide to Tide Pools
items.real_world_notes: For the coast at low tide: ochre stars, giant green anemones, gooseneck barnacles. Look but don't move them.
items.flavor: A small guide to the bright, wet gardens that appear when the tide goes out.

base_weight.definition: Everything in and on the pack except consumables (food, water, fuel). Worn clothing and shoes are not counted.
base_weight.olympic_reality: Olympic adds weight that ultralight lists from drier ranges leave out: a required 2 to 2.75 lb bear canister, real rain pants, and often traction or an ice axe early in the season. A sensible Olympic summer base weight is 14 to 20 lb; a Mount Olympus glacier kit is 25 to 35 lb before food.

consumables.food_lb_per_person_day: 1.5 (dense) to 2.25 (bulky or fresh); plan on about 1.75
consumables.water: 1 L weighs 2.2 lb. Most Olympic trails cross water often, so 1 to 2 L carried is usual; dry stretches (Hoh Lake Trail switchbacks, the High Divide crest in late summer) need 2 to 3 L.
consumables.fuel: About 20 to 30 g of fuel per person per day for boil-only cooking (see food_catalog needs.fuel).

total_load_pct_body_weight.heavy: 25 to 30%: slower pace, sore hips and shoulders, harder fords and ladders
total_load_pct_body_weight.miserable: over 30%: every climb is a grind, footing suffers, knees complain on descents
total_load_pct_body_weight.game_formula: comfortLb = min(pack.comfortable_max_load_lb, 0.25 x bodyLb); r = packWeightLb / comfortLb. Feel: Light r <= 0.6, Comfortable <= 1.0, Heavy <= 1.3, Very heavy <= 1.6, Brutal <= 2.0, above 2.0 you can't leave the car (simulation.md 6.5).

pack_guidance.pack_rating: comfortable_max_load_lb is the load the frame and hip belt carry well. Beyond it, the frame flexes, the hip belt slides and the weight lands on the shoulders. Frameless and framesheet packs fall off sharply past their rating; internal and external frame packs degrade more gently.

volume_fill.rule: insideL = sum of inside items' volume_l (compressed volume when a compression sack is used) + 8% dead space around rigid items. Food rides inside the canister, so food volume counts against the canister's capacity_l, not the pack's.
volume_fill.stuffed: <= 1.10 (slow to pack each morning; the lid barely closes)
volume_fill.wont_close: > 1.10: something comes out or goes outside

what_makes_a_pack_miserable: Load above the pack's comfortable rating, or above about 25% of body weight.
Poor fit: torso length wrong, hip belt riding on the stomach instead of the hip bones.
Heavy items (canister, water, food) far from the back or high in a small pack, which pulls you backward and makes ladders and log crossings wobbly.
A Christmas tree of outside items: they swing, snag on brush and blowdown, soak up rain and fall off.
Water you can't reach without taking the pack off, so you stop drinking.
Wet gear: no liner, so the sleeping bag and dry clothes are damp by camp.
Hard objects poking the back: a canister sideways in a frameless pack, a stove against the spine.
Overstuffing: an 80 L pack filled to the top because the space was there.
Cotton anything that soaks up rain and doubles in weight.

packing_order.bottom: Sleeping bag and sleep clothes in a dry bag (not needed until camp).
packing_order.core_against_back: Heaviest items: bear canister standing upright, water bladder, stove and fuel.
packing_order.top: Puffy, rain gear, water filter, first aid kit, lunch: things you may need during the day.
packing_order.lid_and_hip_belt: Map, compass, phone, snacks, sunscreen, lip balm, headlamp, permit.
packing_order.side_pockets: Water bottles, tent poles, trekking poles when stowed, umbrella.
packing_order.outside_straps: Foam pad, tent in a dry bag, ice axe on the tool loop, crampons in a bag. Only what doesn't fit inside.

pack_guidance.sample_kits: Representative kits computed from this catalog by the build script (food at 1.75 lb and 2.0 L per day; rigid items +8% volume). Design aids, not rules.

day_hike_sensible.description: A well-packed summer day hike (for example Hurricane Hill or Marymere Falls to Storm King's viewpoint).

summer_3_nights_seven_lakes.description: A sensible solo August trip: Sol Duc trailhead, Seven Lakes Basin, the High Divide and back.

olympus_blue_glacier_5_nights.description: A well-equipped July climb: Hoh trailhead to Glacier Meadows, summit day across the Blue Glacier, two partners sharing rope and rescue gear (this carrier holds the rope).

olympus_day_gear_one_night_TRAP.description: The user's warning case: Glacier Meadows in one night with a day-hike kit and a borrowed canister. Note how nothing for the night fits.

loop_in_a_day_3l.description: Ambitious but equipped (F.1): the High Divide loop in a day, 18.4 mi and about 4,400 ft, with a headlamp and spare batteries, 3 L of water (a 2-L bladder and a 1-L bottle, filled again at Deer Lake or Heart Lake), poles and a warm layer for a late finish on the crest. No canister: a day hike needs none.
loop_in_a_day_3l.used_by: F.1 row "Ambitious but equipped": the loop in a day with headlamp and 3 L

day_gear_TRAP_no_canister.description: The canonical day-gear trap kit as a day hike carries it (F.1, the first playable's trap): no headlamp, one liter, cotton, a brochure map, and no canister, since a day hike takes none. Same clothes and bag as olympus_day_gear_one_night_TRAP.
day_gear_TRAP_no_canister.used_by: F.1 rows "The first playable's trap" (Bold and Cautious bots)

pack_guidance.sample_kits_computed_note: loop_in_a_day_3l and day_gear_TRAP_no_canister were added 2026-10-08 (M1A_DATA_CHECK item 23) with the same method: base weight is the pack plus carried items (consumables like fuel excluded); total adds water at 2.2 lb per liter and the day's food; load ratio is total over the pack's comfortable maximum. The phone is worn (pocket) in the loop kit. These two and the four above become rules/kits.json test kits at ingest.

rentals: BEAR CANISTERS: required for every wilderness overnight in Olympic in 2026 (park-approved hard-sided containers; soft sacks and hangs do not count). The Port Angeles Wilderness Information Center lends canisters free, first come, first served (the Quinault station was closed in 2026). In game: canister_wic_loaner; the ranger desk always has one to lend (GAME_DESIGN Lead call 33), though the real WIC says it occasionally runs out over exceptionally busy weekends. Outfitters typically rent canisters for about $4 to $6 a day or $15 to $25 a week, carbon canisters about $7 a day; buying ($80 to $95) beats renting after about three trips. SNOW AND GLACIER GEAR: outfitters in Port Angeles, Sequim and Seattle-area shops rent ice axes (about $10/day), steel crampons (about $15/day), mountaineering boots (about $25 to $35/day), helmets and harnesses (about $8/day each), glacier rope (about $20/day), crevasse rescue kits (about $15/day), avalanche beacon-probe-shovel sets (about $25/day), snowshoes (about $15/day) and slip-on traction chains (about $5/day, though most people just buy them). Deposits and ID are required, stock is limited on summer weekends (in game, roll availability and cap at 2 or 3 glacier sets), pickup happens during store hours the day before (which can push back the drive and the trailhead start), and late returns cost an extra day. Items with stats.rent_usd_per_day are rentable. SKILLS ARE NOT RENTABLE: an ice axe only helps if you can self-arrest, and a rope only helps a trained team of two or more. Most people who reach the summit of Mount Olympus go with experienced partners or a guide, and many turn back at the Blue Glacier's lateral moraine. OTHER: tide tables cost about $2 at outfitters and visitor-center shops. The permit is bought online or at the WIC, not at a store. There is no gear rental inside the park, so anything forgotten after the last-chance store stays forgotten.

tag_glossary.adjustable_torso: Fits a range of torso lengths (fewer fit complaints).
tag_glossary.backup: Good backup for a primary item.
tag_glossary.bear_resistant_soft: Soft animal-resistant sack (not approved in Olympic).
tag_glossary.bombproof: Never fails from wear: the general store's heavy, plain gear, such as the canvas tarp and the foam pads (GAME_DESIGN 5.2, 5.7; replaces unbreakable, 2026-10-09).
tag_glossary.brush_protection: Protects legs from brush, nettles and devil's club.
tag_glossary.bulky: Unusually large packed volume for its job.
tag_glossary.caffeine_ritual: Morning coffee ritual; joy at breakfast.
tag_glossary.camp_comfort: Makes camp more comfortable; joy at camp.
tag_glossary.camp_shoes: Counts as camp_shoes (feet recover at camp).
tag_glossary.camp_water: Lets you carry water to a dry camp.
tag_glossary.coast: Mainly useful on the wilderness coast.
tag_glossary.compressible: Packs smaller in a compression sack.
tag_glossary.cotton: Cotton: no warmth when wet, slow to dry.
tag_glossary.cotton_canvas: Canvas pack body that soaks up rain.
tag_glossary.daypack: Pack meant for day hikes; no room for an overnight kit plus canister.
tag_glossary.down: Down fill: warmest per ounce, nearly useless when soaked.
tag_glossary.emergency_shelter: Emergency-only shelter for an unplanned night.
tag_glossary.expedition: Very large pack for glacier, winter or long trips.
tag_glossary.external_frame: Old-style exposed aluminum frame: carries heavy loads, snags, sways on ladders.
tag_glossary.fastpack: Small, light pack for minimalist one- or two-night trips.
tag_glossary.field_guide: Counts as field_guide (names plants and animals).
tag_glossary.flotation: Keeps you on top of deep snow.
tag_glossary.flower_press: For pressing picked flowers (picking is prohibited).
tag_glossary.footwear_casual: Street shoes, not made for trail.
tag_glossary.footwear_mountaineering: Stiff boots for crampons and snow.
tag_glossary.four_season: Built for snow, wind and cold.
tag_glossary.fragile: Can break, tear or puncture; damage rolls apply.
tag_glossary.freeze_sensitive: Can be damaged invisibly by freezing.
tag_glossary.gaiters: Keeps debris, snow or water out of footwear.
tag_glossary.glacier_travel: Part of a glacier kit (Blue Glacier, Snow Dome).
tag_glossary.group: Most efficient when shared by a group.
tag_glossary.hang: Food-hanging gear (hangs not acceptable in Olympic in 2026).
tag_glossary.hatchet: A hatchet (cutting live vegetation is prohibited).
tag_glossary.hygiene: Hygiene item; reduces illness or improves comfort.
tag_glossary.knee_saver: Eases steep descents on the knees.
tag_glossary.light_phone: Phone flashlight as a weak light source.
tag_glossary.lnt_noise: Creates noise that breaks Leave No Trace etiquette.
tag_glossary.luxury: Not needed for safety; adds joy.
tag_glossary.nav_compass: Counts as nav:compass (with a map: nav:map_compass).
tag_glossary.nav_compass_poor: A toy compass: rough direction only.
tag_glossary.nav_gps_if_maps: Counts as nav:gps if offline maps are present and the battery lasts.
tag_glossary.nav_map_poor: A map too vague for route finding (navigation checks get no bonus).
tag_glossary.needs_battery: Stops working when its battery runs out.
tag_glossary.needs_fuel_canister: Needs a fuel canister to work.
tag_glossary.needs_partner: Only useful with at least one trained companion.
tag_glossary.needs_trees: Needs two trees; useless above treeline and on beaches.
tag_glossary.no_hipbelt: All weight rides on the shoulders.
tag_glossary.no_shutoff_fire_ban: No shut-off valve; usually banned under Stage 2 fire restrictions.
tag_glossary.not_park_approved: Does not meet Olympic's 2026 food-storage rule.
tag_glossary.pack_out: Leaves trash that must be packed out.
tag_glossary.poncho: Poncho: covers the pack too; flaps in wind.
tag_glossary.pre_trip: Applied at home before the trip; weighs nothing on the trail.
tag_glossary.prohibited: Use is against park rules; ranger and LNT consequences.
tag_glossary.puncture_risk: Can puncture (especially strapped outside in brush).
tag_glossary.quick_dry: Dries within a couple of hours.
tag_glossary.rechargeable: Battery can be recharged from a power bank or panel.
tag_glossary.required_overnight: Required by park rules for any overnight.
tag_glossary.rigid: Hard-shelled; adds dead space when packed (8% of volume).
tag_glossary.sand_snow_anchor: Holds in sand and soft snow.
tag_glossary.shallow_source_ok: Can draw from shallow seeps and puddles.
tag_glossary.sharp: Sharp points; can damage other gear if packed carelessly.
tag_glossary.shelter_accessory: Improves a shelter; not a shelter itself.
tag_glossary.shelter_tarp: Counts as shelter:tarp (open sides, no bug protection).
tag_glossary.shutoff_valve: Has an on/off valve; allowed under most fire bans.
tag_glossary.side_pocket: Rides in a pack side pocket.
tag_glossary.sketchbook: Counts as sketchbook. The journal system was retired on 2026-10-08: the tag maps to the luxury event tag (GAME_DESIGN E.4).
tag_glossary.slow_drying: Takes many hours to dry; stays wet in Olympic humidity.
tag_glossary.smellable: Scented item that must go in the bear canister at night.
tag_glossary.snags: Catches on brush and blowdown; extra snag rolls.
tag_glossary.solar: Recharges from sunlight (weak under canopy and fog).
tag_glossary.storm_worthy: Holds up in a full storm.
tag_glossary.stove: Counts as stove (hot food and drink, boiling water).
tag_glossary.stove_liquid: Burns white gas; reliable in cold.
tag_glossary.style: The look, with little or no effect on the trail: the boutique's style items (GAME_DESIGN 5.2, 5.7; added 2026-10-09, no M1a item carries it yet).
tag_glossary.sun_glasses: Eye protection from sun and snow glare.
tag_glossary.synthetic: Synthetic fiber: dries fast, keeps some warmth when wet.
tag_glossary.trap: A realistic mistake: the item works against you on most Olympic trips (notes explain why).
tag_glossary.ultralight: Unusually light for its job; often less durable.
tag_glossary.umbrella: Umbrella: great in calm rain, useless in wind.
tag_glossary.ventilated_back: Mesh back panel; less sweaty in heat.
tag_glossary.versatile: Has several uses; event cards may offer it as an alternative.
tag_glossary.vintage: Old-fashioned gear with charm and drawbacks.
tag_glossary.water_treat_uv: Counts as water_treat:uv (fails in silty or tannic water).
tag_glossary.waterproof_fabric: Pack fabric sheds rain; seams can still leak.
tag_glossary.waterproofing_item: Keeps one bundle of gear dry.
tag_glossary.wet_sensitive: Loses most warmth when wet; keep it dry.
tag_glossary.winter: Mainly useful in winter and spring snow.
tag_glossary.wool: Wool: stays somewhat warm when wet, resists odor.

stat_glossary.temp_rating_f: Sleeping bag or quilt lower-limit rating in °F (most sleepers want 10 °F of margin; see comfort_f).
stat_glossary.comfort_f: Temperature at which a typical sleeper is comfortable in the bag.
stat_glossary.wet_warmth_retained: Fraction of insulating value kept when soaked (down about 0.25, synthetic about 0.6, wool about 0.5, cotton 0).
stat_glossary.compressed_volume_l: Volume in a compression sack (see compression_sack).
stat_glossary.r_value: Sleeping pad thermal resistance. R 2 summer, R 3 to 4 three-season, R 5+ snow. R values add when pads are stacked.
stat_glossary.insulation: Warmth points of a garment, summed across worn layers for the evening warmth model (simulation.md 3 and 7).
stat_glossary.covers: Body zones a garment protects: torso, legs, head, hands, feet, neck, pack.
stat_glossary.dry_time_h: Hours to dry from soaked while worn or hung in mild, dry air.
stat_glossary.wind_block: 0 to 3: how well a garment stops wind.
stat_glossary.rain_rating: 0 to 3 for shelters and shells: how much rain gets through. 3 = storm-proof.
stat_glossary.wind_rating: 0 to 3 for shelters: how well it stands up to gusts.
stat_glossary.breathability: 0 to 3: how quickly sweat escapes (low values mean damp from the inside).
stat_glossary.condensation: 0 to 3 for shelters: how wet the inside gets on still, humid nights (0 = none, tarp).
stat_glossary.warmth_bonus_f: Degrees F added to the sleep system's effective rating (tents trap a few degrees; hammocks lose some from below).
stat_glossary.capacity_people: How many sleepers a shelter holds.
stat_glossary.capacity_l: Usable inside volume of a container (canister, pot, dry bag).
stat_glossary.usable_l: Canister volume that food actually fills (about 85% of capacity_l because round walls leave dead space).
stat_glossary.person_days_typical: Days of food for one person that fit at about 2.0 L of food per day (see food_catalog bear_can_capacity).
stat_glossary.approved_olympic_2026: Whether the container is on the park-approved list for 2026.
stat_glossary.full_volume_l: Pack volume a water container takes when full.
stat_glossary.wait_min: Minutes before chemically treated water is safe for most pathogens.
stat_glossary.fuel_g: Grams of fuel in a canister or bottle.
stat_glossary.boils_0_5l_mild: Half-liter boils per container at about 60 °F with no wind (fewer in cold and wind).
stat_glossary.fuel_g_per_l_boil: Grams of fuel to bring 1 L to a boil in mild, calm conditions.
stat_glossary.boil_min_per_l: Minutes to boil 1 L in mild conditions.
stat_glossary.battery_h_low: Hours of light on the low setting.
stat_glossary.traction: 0 to 5 grip on snow and ice (shoes 0 to 3, traction chains 3, crampons 4 to 5).
stat_glossary.ankle_support: 0 to 3; reduces sprain chance on rough trail with a heavy pack.
stat_glossary.blister_risk: 0 to 3 (lower is better); liner socks are negative.
stat_glossary.ford_ok: Safe to wear across a river ford.
stat_glossary.loss_in_current: Chance a shoe is swept away when worn across a strong ford.
stat_glossary.joy: Spirits bonus per evening while carried and used.
stat_glossary.joy_layover: Spirits bonus on a layover day.
stat_glossary.joy_rain_day: Spirits bonus on a tent-bound rain day.
stat_glossary.journal_points: Retired with the journal system on 2026-10-08; ingest drops it (GAME_DESIGN E.4). It was credit for recording a discovery: full for a sketch, partial for a photo.
stat_glossary.journal_points_bonus: Added to journal_points when used with a sketchbook or journal.
stat_glossary.rent_usd_per_day: Typical rental price per day; the item can be rented in town.
stat_glossary.wet_chance_mult: Multiplier on the chance that inside gear gets damp in rain or a fall in a ford.
stat_glossary.neighbors_annoyed: Chance per evening that nearby campers are bothered (LNT card).
stat_glossary.citation_chance: Chance per use that a ranger issues a citation.
stat_glossary.min_party: Minimum party size for the item to work.
stat_glossary.self_arrest: Lets the hiker stop a slide on steep snow, if the snow skill is high enough.
stat_glossary.skill_needed: Skill that must be at least 2 for full effect.
stat_glossary.needs: Other items required for the item to be used.
stat_glossary.battery_h: Hours of use on a full battery (or a fresh set).
stat_glossary.battery_days: Trail days on one charge at typical use (estimate); cold shortens it.
stat_glossary.battery_shots: Photos per charge, from the CIPA rating class for the camera type (estimate).
stat_glossary.battery_type: Battery the item needs, for the spare-battery and charging checks.

night_model_stats.rule: The night model (GAME_DESIGN 7.9) and the cause trace (8.13) read each item's own stats: warmth_bonus_f for shelters and wet_warmth_retained for insulation. The doc's flat figures are only fallbacks for an item that lacks the stat (M1A_DATA_CHECK item 5, settled 2026-10-08).
night_model_stats.coverage: Every shelter has warmth_bonus_f (footprint and stakes are accessories), and since 2026-10-08 every insulating clothing item has wet_warmth_retained, so the fallbacks are never used for catalog items.
night_model_stats.doc_examples: The 7.9 and 8.13 worked examples should be regenerated from these stats as F.4 goldens (doc owner).
